title: Grid Systems Consultant
description:
GRID SYSTEMS CONSULTANT

Location: Kansas City, MO
Job type: 1 Year Contract

Our client is seeking a Grid Systems Consultant to support the delivery of comprehensive grid management systems consulting services for electric utility clients. The primary responsibility of this role is to contribute to the successful execution of the service offerings to modernize operations, enhance reliability, and adopt advanced grid technologies for a resilient, future-ready grid.

The Grid Systems Consultant will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to assist clients through every phase of their modernization journey, from strategy development, capability assessment, and business case analysis to requirements definition, RFP development, software selection, and program management. This position will also support system integration and implementation services, including the design, build, testing, and deployment of advanced technology solutions in Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), Outage Management Systems (OMS), Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), and Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS).

Key responsibilities also include gathering and analyzing client requirements, supporting the development of project roadmaps, facilitating workshops, preparing technical documentation, and providing operational support post-deployment.

Success in this role requires foundational knowledge of grid management technologies, strong analytical and communication skills, and the ability to work collaboratively in a client-facing environment. The Grid Systems Consultant plays a vital part in ensuring project quality, upholding best practices, and embracing continuous improvement, ultimately helping utilities realize sustainable, innovative outcomes in their transformation programs.

RESPONSIBLITIES
  • Support the delivery and implementation of SCADA, EMS, OMS, DMS, ADMS, and DERMS solutions under the direction of senior team members, contributing to client modernization and operations improvement efforts.
  • Assist in commissioning, testing, and deployment activities for grid management systems, following established processes and industry best practices
  • Contribute to troubleshooting, field support, and project coordination activities aimed at optimizing and maintaining advanced grid systems and applications (e.g., FLISR, VVO, DER integration).
  • Participate in requirements gathering, data analysis, and business process documentation to inform the design and configuration of client solutions.
  • Collaborate on project planning, budgeting, and execution tasks—supporting the development of detailed project plans, tracking milestones, and preparing documentation for status updates.
  • Contribute to analysis, design, build, configuration, and testing activities across project lifecycles, including defect triage and deployment support.
  • Assist with project management activities such as scheduling, communication, and task tracking using methodologies like Waterfall or Agile, as directed.
  • Prepare and maintain quality deliverables, technical documentation, and client presentations, ensuring alignment with project goals and company standards.
  • Support the facilitation of workshops, meetings, and training sessions with clients and project stakeholders.
  • Aid in the development and implementation of change management and business process design activities, incorporating feedback from stakeholders to address operational needs.
  • Assist with software selection activities, including requirements definition, RFP development, vendor evaluation, and solution demonstrations.
  • Help to ensure compliance with company safety protocols and site policies.
  • Contribute to operational support and post-deployment activities, including training, documentation updates, and ongoing client assistance.
  • Foster teamwork and maintain effective communication with internal teams, clients, and vendors.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support project delivery, team objectives, and client success.
REQUIREMENTS
  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field from an accredited program and min 8 years of relevant experience is required.
  • Minimum 8 years working in the Electric Utility Industry or equivalent.
  • Experience with electric utility clients implementing and integrating operational systems such as OMS, DMS, ADMS, AMI, Distribution Automation, and Distributed Energy Resources (DER) is preferred.
  • Preferred: Experience with the AspenTech monarch platform.
  • Strong ability to influence or lead project execution.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience with leading-edge applications (s), operations technology, and solutions utilizing various industry standard tools.
  • Experience with a variety of project execution methodologies, including but not limited to Waterfall and Agile.

title: Plant Superintendent
description:
Job Title: Plant Superintendent
Location: Winchester, KY (Relocation assistance provided)
Job Type and Duration: Direct Hire/Permanent position
Pay range: $119k - $134k plus bonus

Reporting directly to the Plant Manager, as a Plant Superintendent, the position is accountable for safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost performance, employee training and relations in a high-performance work team environment, capital improvements and budget preparation in a 24/7 plastics manufacturing facility. This job demands monitoring production performance and implementing processes, procedures, and methods to improve results in all key functional areas. Position is responsible for implementing and maintaining best manufacturing practices and regulatory compliance for all production activities.

What you'll be doing:
  • Ensure the safety of all employees; lead a comprehensive safety program to prevent injuries. Comply with all federal, state, and local environmental and safety regulations (EPA, OSHA, etc.).
  • Develop subordinates through education, training, and teamwork.
  • Is responsible for motivation, support and guidance to all employees
  • Communicate problems and obstacles to the plant manager and the leadership team. Establish workflow policies that enhance speed and efficiency without compromising safety, product safety or integrity
  • Create schedules for employees to ensure optimum staffing levels
  • Assist in preparation of annual plant operating budget. Meet or exceed plant productivity, cost, or other performance metric expectations as outlined by plant manager.
  • Assist in employee relations issues
  • Hire, train, direct and mentor staff and all plant employees with diverse cultural and educational background.
  • Lead plant in continuous improvement initiatives, such as 5S with safety, 6 Sigma, Kaizen events, and lean manufacturing.
  • Coordinate production scheduling to meet customer demands, to manage overtime, to minimize inventory, and to reduce costs.
  • Support quality initiatives to ensure product meets or exceeds customer expectations. Ensure employees complete required quality checks and audits.
  • Build and maintain productive employee relationships, driving employee satisfaction. Provide direction, training, and development as needed. Provide coaching, counseling, or discipline as needed. Recommend disciplinary action to plant manager and review disciplinary action by supervisors for effectiveness and consistency. Work with HR to address employee concerns and issues.
  • Identify, propose, and implement capital projects to improve operational performance.

This position is in our Winchester, KY plant.

We'd love to hear from you if you:
  • Have a Bachelor's degree or higher education. Engineering and/or plastics major with experience preferred
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of manufacturing experience or equivalent
  • Proven track record of successful leadership positions
  • You can demonstrate a history of a strong work ethic
  • Comfortable in public speaking and training large groups of coworkers.
  • Must have above average communication skills (written & verbal in English)
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint to include creating charts, graphs, SOP's, One Point Lessons, presentations
  • Must have high level of integrity, trust, and ethical standards
  • Must be able and willing to work overtime and flexible schedule as needed to support all shifts

Work Environment:
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts in a production environment. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud. Temperatures inside the plant can fluctuate between hot and cold according to seasonal changes. Personal protective equipment (PPE) is required in the production department and other designated areas.

Compensation:
The annual base salary range for this role is from $119,760 to $134,730, plus annual target bonus of 12.5% of base salary. Incentive is a target of 12.5% with ability to earn up to 25% paid on a quarterly basis.
